mainTopic: Believing a person who denies the עדים, how lapses of awareness, dishes and half-measures combine into a חטאת, and the time limit for one act of eating
overview: The amud opens by asking why a person who denies being טמא is treated differently from someone who denies eating חלב or entering the מקדש. רבינא explains that 'I never became impure' cannot be reread as 'I already immersed.' רב נחמן rules like רבי יהודה that a person is believed about himself, and רב יוסף limits this to how he treats himself. Then ריש לקיש, רב ששת and אביי each give a case where even רבי מאיר agrees the denier is believed, because he could have made another claim that would exempt him anyway. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. אביי teaches that separate lapses of awareness (העלמות) mean separate חטאות. ריש לקיש explains the half-כזית cases through רבי יהושע's rule that separate dishes divide the eating, in two versions with opposite results. רבינא explains the first line through רבן גמליאל's view that awareness does not split a half-measure. Finally, a new משנה sets the time limit for eating, כדי אכילת פרס. The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר's 'קליות' measure is meant to be strict or lenient, and it begins a proof from the wording of the חכמים that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If it is old impurity, why can't he explain his denial too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the case is about טומאה ישנה. In that case the person could also reinterpret his denial, just like with חלבים and ביאת מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the case is old impurity, what is different about חלבים and entering the מקדש, where the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה because he could say 'I did it on purpose'? With old impurity he can also explain his words: he could say 'I didn't stay impure, I immersed!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking one way of explaining the ברייתא. It argues that a person with old impurity can also 'fix' his denial, so the חכמים should exempt him here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חלבים and ביאת מקדש, his denial is not a true contradiction of the עדים, because he could mean 'it wasn't by accident, it was on purpose.' If the impurity happened earlier (like yesterday), 'I wasn't impure' could mean 'I wasn't impure anymore, since I went to the מקוה.' So the reason the חכמים gave for exempting him in the other cases seems to apply here as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Old impurity: the person became טמא some time earlier, so he had a chance to immerse
Forbidden fats of an animal
Entering the מקדש (while טמא)
On purpose; a person who sins on purpose does not bring a חטאת
He can explain his statement in a way that fits with the עדים
I immersed (in a מקוה), so I became טהור

steps.confusionAlert: Being exempt here is not about the person being believed over the עדים. It is about his words being read so they don't really contradict the עדים at all.

phrases.english: [If you say it is talking] about old impurity,
phrases.notes: 'Old' impurity means he became impure earlier, for example yesterday.

phrases.english: what is different about forbidden fats and entering the Temple
where they agree with him,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the חכמים, and 'him' is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: since if he wished he could say: 'I did it on purpose'?
With old impurity too, he can explain his statement,
since if he wished he could say:
'I did not stay in my impurity; rather, I immersed!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous discussion by testing the 'old impurity' reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא, where the חכמים hold him liable, is talking about טומאה ישנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same 'he can reinterpret his words' reason that exempts him for חלבים and ביאת מקדש applies to old impurity, because 'I'm not impure' can mean 'I already immersed.'

steps.title: רבינא: the witnesses said he ate קדשים while impure
steps.stepSummary: רבינא keeps the case as old impurity, but describes it so the person cannot reinterpret his words: the עדים say he ate קדשים while טמא, and he answers 'I never became impure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It really is old impurity, but the case is where עדים tell him 'You ate קדשים while your body was impure,' and he tells them 'I never became impure.' Here he cannot explain his statement, because he cannot claim 'I didn't stay impure, I immersed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. He keeps 'old impurity' but sets up the exact wording of the claims so that no reinterpretation is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is what the person actually said. He did not say 'I'm not impure now.' He said 'I never became impure' (לא נטמאתי). That wording denies the impurity itself, so 'I immersed' cannot fit into it.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really: keeps the original explanation and adds a detail
Sacred food, like meat of קרבנות
Impurity of the person's body
I did not become impure (a denial of ever becoming impure)

phrases.english: Ravina said: Actually, it is about old impurity,
and the case is where witnesses say to him:
You ate sacred food while your body was impure,
and he says to them: 'I did not become impure,'
for here he cannot explain his statement.
For one cannot say
'I did not stay impure, but I immersed,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (the exact wording of the claims)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought any denial of old impurity could be read as 'I already immersed.'
steps.terutzMaskana: When he says 'I never became impure' in answer to 'you ate קדשים while impure,' his words cannot be reinterpreted, so the עדים contradict him and he is liable.

steps.title: Why 'I immersed and ate' doesn't save his statement
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains further. Even if he says 'I immersed and then ate,' that admits he had been impure from touching something, which contradicts his first claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would he say to them, 'I immersed and then ate'? Once he says that, his first statement 'I never became impure' is shown to be false, at least about the impurity he got from touching.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא proves his answer by trying out the only possible reinterpretation and showing that it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To use 'I immersed,' he has to admit he was impure before. But his first words were 'I never became impure.' So 'I immersed' does not explain his first statement. It cancels it.

keyTerms.meaning: Was contradicted, shown to be false
His first statement
Impurity he got by touching something impure

steps.whatToRemember: A denial can be 'explained' only if the new explanation fits his actual words. 'I never became impure' cannot be stretched to mean 'I immersed.'

phrases.english: What would he say to them?
'I immersed and then I ate'?
When he says this to them,
his first statement has been contradicted
at least regarding his impurity from touching!
phrases.notes: Saying 'I immersed' admits he once touched something impure, which is exactly what 'I never became impure' denied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבינא's answer by showing that the possible reinterpretation fails.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the reinterpretation contradicts his own words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe 'I immersed and ate' could save him.
steps.terutzMaskana: It doesn't, because it admits the impurity from touching that he had denied.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: a person is believed that he is טהור, even against עדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from analyzing the ברייתא to giving the practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה held that a person who says 'I did not become impure' is believed about himself even against עדים. רב נחמן makes this the הלכה, against the חכמים who hold him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analysis to the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person is believed to say he is טהור, even against עדים, like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: only for himself
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף limits רבי יהודה's view. The person is believed only for his own sake, not to make others treat him as טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי יהודה said it only between him and himself, and for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a limit to the ruling just given. The person is believed only for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Believing the person does not cancel the עדים for everyone. He may treat himself as טהור, but other people still treat him as טמא based on the עדים.

keyTerms.meaning: Between him and himself, in private
For himself only, not for others

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being believed can be personal: the same person can be considered טהור for himself and טמא for others.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, but according to רב יוסף his trust is only for himself; others go by the עדים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לֹא אֲמָרָהּ [רַבִּי יְהוּדָה]
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: [Rabbi Yehuda] said it only
phrases.notes: The name in square brackets is in the corrected wording, to make clear who 'he' is.

phrases.english: between him and himself, and for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לֹא אֲמָרָהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far רב נחמן's ruling goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's trust in the person applies only to how he treats himself, not to how others treat him.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי מאיר agrees in the case of the designated maidservant
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים in the case of שפחה חרופה. If the man denies the עדים, he is believed, because he could have said he never finished the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: רבי מאיר agrees with the Rabbis that if two witnesses tell a man, 'You had relations with a designated maidservant,' and he says, 'I did not,' he is believed. If he had wanted to, he could have told them, 'I did not complete the act.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש names a case where even רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים that the person is believed against the עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר usually holds that two עדים obligate a person to bring a קרבן even if he denies it. With שפחה חרופה, though, he is only obligated if he finished the act. So his 'I did not' can be read as 'I did not finish,' and that claim exempts him even if the עדים are right.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees (here: רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים in this case)
A maidservant who is designated (betrothed) to a Hebrew slave; relations with her bring an אשם
He is believed
Since if he wanted, he could have said: the reason a person's word is trusted
Completing the act of relations

steps.confusionAlert: He is not saying the עדים are lying. He could even agree with what they saw. His denial is believed because the claim he could make, 'I did not finish,' leaves him with no obligation either way.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Rabbi Meir agrees with the Rabbis
that if two [witnesses] said to him:
You had relations with a designated maidservant,
and he says: I did not have relations –
he is believed,
since if he wanted, he could say to them:
I did not complete my act of relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the idea from Step 1, that a denial can be read as a different claim, to define a case where רבי מאיר agrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שפחה חרופה, even רבי מאיר holds the denier is believed, since he could claim he did not finish the act.

steps.title: רב ששת: רבי מאיר agrees in the case of the impure nazirite
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says רבי מאיר agrees that a נזיר who denies becoming טמא is exempt, because he could have said his נזירות was annulled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת says: רבי מאיר agrees with the Rabbis about a nazirite whom two witnesses tell, 'You became impure,' and he says, 'I did not become impure.' He is exempt, because if he had wanted to, he could have said, 'I asked to have my nazirite vow annulled.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second case where רבי מאיר agrees the person is believed, this time with a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who becomes טמא must bring קרבנות. If he had his vow annulled by a חכם, he was no longer a נזיר, so becoming טמא was allowed. Because he could have made that claim, his plain 'I did not become impure' is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became impure (from a dead body), who must bring קרבנות
Exempt (from the קרבן)
I asked (a חכם) about my נזירות, meaning: I had my vow annulled

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר לַחֲכָמִים בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir agrees with the Rabbis about an impure nazirite,
to whom two [witnesses] said: You became impure,
and he says: I did not become impure –
he is exempt,
since if he wanted, he could say:
I asked about my nazirite vow.
phrases.notes: He means a חכם annulled his vow, so he was no longer a נזיר and was allowed to become טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר לַחֲכָמִים בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel case to ריש לקיש's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא נזיר who denies the עדים is exempt even according to רבי מאיר, since he could claim his vow was annulled.

steps.title: אביי: רבי מאיר agrees in the case of knowing testimony
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי מאיר agrees that a person who denies knowing testimony is exempt, because he could have said he never meant to serve as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: רבי מאיר agrees with the Rabbis that if two witnesses tell someone, 'You know testimony about so-and-so,' and he says, 'I did not know,' he is exempt. If he had wanted to, he could have said, 'I did not intend to be a witness.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a third case where רבי מאיר agrees, this time about someone who denies knowing testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about someone who denies (with an oath) knowing testimony. He would bring a קרבן for falsely denying it. He could have said he saw the event but never intended to serve as a witness, and that claim would exempt him. So his plain denial is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony
So-and-so, someone
I did not intend to be a witness

steps.whatToRemember: All three אמוראים follow one rule. Even רבי מאיר believes the person against two עדים whenever he could have made a different claim that would exempt him anyway.

phrases.english: Abaye says:
Rabbi Meir agrees with the Rabbis
that if two [witnesses] said to him:
You know testimony about so-and-so,
and he says: I did not know –
he is exempt,
since if he wanted, he could say:
I did not intend to be a witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר לַחֲכָמִים, שֶׁאִם אָמְרוּ לוֹ שְׁנַיִם: יוֹדֵעַ אַתָּה בְּעֵדוּת פְּלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of cases where רבי מאיר agrees with the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who denies knowing testimony is exempt even according to רבי מאיר, since he could claim he never intended to be a witness.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: eating forbidden fat twice in one lapse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: someone who ate חלב and then more חלב during one העלם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: one who ate forbidden fat and then more forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness brings only one sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new line. This sets up the next move, רבי זירא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. The משנה rules that two כזיתים of חלב eaten during the same lapse of awareness need only one חטאת. The quote gives us the ruling that רבי זירא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat; eating it by mistake requires a חטאת
One lapse of awareness, with no remembering in between

phrases.english: If he ate forbidden fat and [again] forbidden fat
during one lapse of awareness.
phrases.notes: Some versions say אַחַת and some say אֶחָד. Both just mean 'one'; the square brackets show the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of believing a denier and moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two eatings of חלב in one lapse of awareness need only one חטאת.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks why only one sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges the משנה. The person ate two separate כזיתים of חלב, so why does he bring only one חטאת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Why does he bring only one sin offering? He ate two olive-sizes of forbidden fat!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the משנה's ruling of only one חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כזית is the amount that makes a person obligated, and here he ate two full ones. Each looks like a complete sin of its own, so we would expect two חטאות. The question is why one lapse of awareness joins them into one.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it: a strong challenge
Olive-sizes: the amount of eating that makes one obligated
Sin offering, brought for doing a sin by mistake

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to this:
Why is he not liable
except for one sin offering?
But he ate two olive-sizes of forbidden fat!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: אַמַּאי אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה line quoted in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that two eatings of חלב in one העלם need only one חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each כזית is a complete amount for obligation, so two כזיתים should mean two separate sins and two חטאות.

steps.title: אביי: Only separate lapses of awareness create two offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבי זירא. Two חטאות are brought only when there are separate lapses of awareness, and here there was just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Two offerings come only with separate lapses of awareness, but here there is only one lapse of awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא's question from Step 10. Even though the person ate two כזיתים of חלב, he did it during one העלם, so he brings only one חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא thought that two separate amounts of חלב should mean two offerings. אביי explains that what counts is not how many כזיתים were eaten but how many lapses of awareness there were. One העלם covers everything eaten during it, so there is one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A lapse of awareness: the time when the person did not know or forgot that the food was forbidden

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי זירא, who asked the question in the previous step.

phrases.english: [Two offerings come only with] separate lapses of awareness,
but here there is only one lapse of awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the real factor: the number of lapses of awareness, not the number of כזיתים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two separate כזיתים of חלב should mean two חטאות
steps.terutzMaskana: One העלם covers all the eating, so there is one חטאת

steps.title: Second version: Why should two lapses matter if it is all one kind of fat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a different version of רבי זירא's question. He infers from the משנה that two lapses of awareness would mean two offerings, and he asks why, since it is all the same prohibition of חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who pose the challenge this way: The reason he brings only one is that it was one lapse of awareness. This implies that with two lapses he would bring two. But why? It is all one category of חלב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second version of רבי זירא's question to אביי. In this version he attacks from the opposite direction: why should two lapses of awareness ever create two offerings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי זירא wanted more offerings, because there were two כזיתים. Here he wants fewer: the משנה hints that two העלמות would mean two חטאות. He asks why, since the person broke only one prohibition, the prohibition of חלב.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; used to point out what a ruling depends on
But this implies; it draws the opposite case out of a ruling
Why? It introduces a challenge
One category (literally, one name) of the prohibition of חלב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version רבי זירא asks why there is only ONE offering. In this version he asks why there should ever be TWO.

phrases.english: There are those who pose the challenge this way:
The reason [he brings one] is that it was one lapse of awareness,
which implies that in two lapses of awareness he is liable to two.
Why? It is one category of חלב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the challenge that was answered in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that two העלמות would require two חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one prohibition (חלב) was broken, so the number of lapses should not multiply the offerings

steps.title: אביי: Separate lapses do split the offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that separate lapses of awareness do create separate obligations, even when it is the same prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Separate lapses of awareness divide the offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: In this second version, אביי answers that separate lapses of awareness really do create separate חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though it is one prohibition, each new lapse of awareness starts a new count. So a person who ate חלב, found out, then forgot again and ate more, brings two חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate lapses of awareness split the acts into separate obligations
Sin offerings (plural)
Becoming aware of the sin; this is what separates one lapse from the next

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the rule is the same: one העלם means one חטאת, and separate העלמות mean separate חטאות, even for the same prohibition of חלב.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Separate lapses of awareness divide [the offerings].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second version of רבי זירא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: States a principle: separate lapses of awareness count as separate sins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One category of חלב should mean one offering no matter how many lapses
steps.terutzMaskana: Each separate lapse of awareness requires its own חטאת

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה: חלב, דם, פיגול and נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which deals with eating several different forbidden foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If he ate חלב, blood, פיגול and נותר, he is liable for each one, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on and quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about the end of that משנה, which is coming in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are four different prohibitions, so eating all of them in one העלם brings a חטאת for each one. The "etc." stands for the rest of the משנה, including the case of two half-כזיתים, which the גמרא is about to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, which is forbidden to eat
A קרבן made invalid by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten
Meat of a קרבן left over past the time allowed for eating it
Etc.: the rest of the quoted line continues

phrases.english: If he ate חלב and blood,
פיגול and נותר, he is liable, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." hides the part the גמרא is about to ask about: two half-כזיתים of one kind add up and make him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל חֵלֶב וָדָם פִּיגּוּל וְנוֹתָר – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating several different prohibited foods in one העלם brings a separate חטאת for each one

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that two halves of one kind add up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that two half-כזיתים of the same kind make a person liable. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: From one kind he is liable? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the end of the משנה. If he ate two halves of a כזית of the same forbidden food, he simply ate a full כזית, so why does the משנה need to tell us this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to teach something everyone already knows. Two half-כזיתים of the same food clearly add up to a whole כזית. So the גמרא asks what new point the משנה is making.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! A challenge that a ruling teaches nothing new
One type of forbidden food
An olive-size amount, the smallest amount that makes a person liable

phrases.english: From one type he is liable? That is obvious!
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's case of two half-כזיתים eaten in one lapse of awareness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line of the משנה quoted in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that two half-כזיתים of one type make a person liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two halves of the same food obviously make a full כזית, so the ruling seems unnecessary

steps.title: ריש לקיש: He ate from two separate dishes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting בר תוטיני, explains that the משנה is talking about eating the two halves from two separate dishes, following רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר תוטיני: This is a case where he ate them from two dishes, and it follows רבי יהושע, who says that separate dishes divide the acts.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question. The משנה is teaching something new because the two halves came from two different dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that eating from separate dishes counts as separate acts. So we might have thought that a half-כזית from each dish stays separate and does not add up. The משנה teaches that they still join together to make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish or serving bowl
Separate dishes divide the eating into separate acts
According to the opinion of
For example; it introduces the specific case being described

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case of two halves of one kind is not obvious. It is about two separate dishes, and it teaches that even according to רבי יהושע, who says dishes divide the acts, the two halves still add up.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵינִי:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of bar Tutini:
For example, where he ate them from two dishes,
and it follows the opinion of Rabbi Yehoshua,
who says that separate dishes divide [the acts].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵינִי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאֲכָלוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי תַמְחוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by narrowing the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case (two separate dishes) and ties it to the opinion of a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since separate dishes divide the acts, the two half-כזיתים might not combine
steps.terutzMaskana: Even from two dishes, two halves of one type combine to make him liable

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to say he is liable
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's answer continues. Without the משנה, we might think רבי יהושע's 'separate dishes' rule works both ways. The משנה says he is liable, so the rule works only to make things stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that רבי יהושע's rule of separate dishes applies whether it makes things easier or harder. So the משנה teaches that he is liable. This shows that רבי יהושע said his rule only to be strict, not to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's answer. It explains what new lesson the משנה teaches by saying that two half-כזיתים from two dishes make a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that separate dishes split an act of eating into separate acts. If that worked לקולא, the two halves would not join together, and the person would be exempt. The משנה says he is liable, which proves the rule is only used לחומרא.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / I would have thought
Toward leniency, making things easier
Toward stringency, making things stricter
So it teaches us (the new lesson)
Evidently / this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: First version: רבי יהושע's 'separate dishes' rule only makes things stricter. Two half-כזיתים of one kind from two dishes still join, and he is liable.

phrases.english: You might have said:
when Rabbi Yehoshua said (that separate dishes split the eating),
it makes no difference whether it leads to leniency,
and it makes no difference whether it leads to stringency.
So it teaches us that he is liable,
evidently, he said it to be strict,
but to be lenient he did not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes ריש לקיש's answer from step 16 by spelling out the new lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the new lesson (חידוש) of a seemingly obvious line
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's dish rule might work both ways, so the two halves would not join and he would be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is only לחומרא, so the halves join and he is liable.

steps.title: Another version: the question was on the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: Some say the 'that's obvious' question was asked on the last line of the משנה: half-כזיתים from two kinds are exempt. Of course they are, since he never ate a full כזית of one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the question was on the end of the משנה: if the halves came from two kinds, he is exempt. But that's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion. Here the question 'that's obvious!' is aimed at the סיפא of the משנה instead of the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two half-כזיתים of different forbidden foods never add up to a full כזית of one prohibition. So of course he is exempt, and the משנה seems to say something nobody needed to be told.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Kinds / types (of forbidden food)
Exempt, not liable

phrases.english: There are those who say (this was asked) on the last clause:
'From two kinds — he is exempt.'
phrases.notes: This means half a כזית and another half a כזית, eaten in one lapse of awareness.

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the question from step 15 in a second version, aimed at the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line 'from two kinds, exempt'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Half-amounts of different foods cannot combine, so saying he is exempt seems pointless.

steps.title: One kind eaten from two dishes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting בר תוטיני, says the case is one kind of food eaten from two dishes. It follows רבי יהושע, who holds that separate dishes split the eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר תוטיני: the case is where he ate it from two dishes, and it follows רבי יהושע, who says separate dishes count separately.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the same kind of answer as before, but now it explains the סיפא. 'Two kinds' really means two dishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the case is one food eaten as two halves from two dishes, the ruling is no longer obvious. Under רבי יהושע's rule, the separate dishes stop the halves from joining, so he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵינִי:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of bar Tutini:
For example, where he ate it from two dishes,
and it follows Rabbi Yehoshua,
who says separate dishes are counted separately.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵינִי: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאֲכָלוֹ בִּשְׁנֵי תַמְחוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' question of step 18 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is two truly different foods, which makes the ruling obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one food eaten from two dishes, following רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The new lesson: the rule works for leniency too
steps.stepSummary: Without the משנה, we might think רבי יהושע's rule works only לחומרא. The משנה says he is exempt, so it works לקולא as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that רבי יהושע said his rule only to be strict and not to be lenient. So the משנה teaches: from two kinds, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the סיפא is teaching under this second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of step 17. Here the הוה אמינא is that the rule is only לחומרא. Since the משנה says 'exempt', the dish rule must also work to make things easier.

phrases.english: For you might have said:
when Rabbi Yehoshua said (his rule),
he said it to be strict,
but to be lenient he did not say it.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: מִשְּׁנֵי מִינִין פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: So it teaches us: from two kinds, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the new lesson of ריש לקיש's answer in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's rule is only לחומרא, so the halves would join and he would be liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is exempt, so the rule applies לקולא too.

steps.title: What does 'two kinds' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'two kinds' if the case is really one food.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'from two kinds' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It is setting up an explanation of why one food would be called 'two kinds'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the case is one food in two dishes. The wording 'two kinds' seems to contradict that, so the גמרא needs to explain it.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'from two kinds'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the משנה's wording fits ריש לקיש's case from step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה says 'two kinds' when the case is really one food

steps.title: Two dishes are called 'two kinds'
steps.stepSummary: It really is one kind. The משנה calls it 'two kinds' because it was eaten from two dishes. Since the משנה says he is exempt, רבי יהושע's rule works both לקולא and לחומרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is really one kind. Why does the משנה call it two kinds? Because he ate it from two dishes. The משנה says he is exempt, which shows that רבי יהושע's rule applies both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question and draws the conclusion of the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה calls two dishes 'two kinds' because the dishes split the eating the way different foods would. Since the ruling is 'exempt', רבי יהושע's rule must also work לקולא, the opposite of the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: Calls it
And yet it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1 (רישא): the dish rule is only לחומרא. Version 2 (סיפא): the dish rule works both לקולא and לחומרא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. They use the same answer from ריש לקיש but reach opposite conclusions about how far רבי יהושע's rule goes.

phrases.english: It is really from one kind,
so why does it call it 'two kinds'?
Because he ate it from two dishes,
and it teaches: exempt,
evidently, it makes no difference whether it leads to leniency
or whether it leads to stringency
that Rabbi Yehoshua said (his rule).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמִּין אֶחָד הוּא, וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ שְׁנֵי מִינִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 and closes the second version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Two kinds' means one food eaten from two dishes. Since he is exempt, רבי יהושע's rule works both ways.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the second version, separate dishes split the eating both לקולא and לחומרא.

steps.title: The First Line Now Seems Obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the last line is one kind from two dishes, the first line must be one kind from one dish. Then it is obvious that he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the last line is one kind of food eaten from two dishes, the first line must be one kind from one dish. That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from the last line of the משנה back to the first line. Based on how it just read the last line, it now asks why the first line needs to be said at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 explained 'two kinds' in the last line as one food in two dishes. So the first line, 'one kind', must mean one food in one dish. Two half-כזיתים of the same food from the same dish obviously add up to a full כזית, so the first line seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new 'that's obvious' question about the first line of the משנה. It is not about the last line, which was already explained in Steps 18-22.

phrases.english: Since the last clause is one kind and two dishes,
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא just explained the משנה's 'two kinds' in Step 22.

phrases.english: the first clause must be one kind and one dish.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from Step 22 about the last line to work out what the first line means, and then attacks the first line as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first line of the משנה: two half-כזיתים of one kind make him liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case is one food from one dish, the two halves obviously combine, so the line has no reason to be taught.

steps.title: He Became Aware in Between, Following רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the person realized his sin between the two halves. The משנה follows רבן גמליאל, who holds that awareness does not split a half-measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case is where he became aware of his sin in between the two halves. The משנה follows רבן גמליאל, who says awareness does not count for a half-measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question by adding a new detail to the case. After eating the first half-כזית, the person found out he had sinned, and then he forgot and ate the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, finding out about a sin in the middle divides the acts into two separate times of forgetting, and the halves would not combine. רבן גמליאל holds that this awareness means nothing when only a half-measure has been done, so the halves still join and he must bring a חטאת. That is the new point the first line teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: In between, in the middle
Half of the minimum measure needed to be liable

phrases.english: Ravina said:
For example, where he had awareness in between,
and it follows the view of Rabban Gamliel,
who said: There is no awareness for a half-measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ יְדִיעָה בֵּינְתַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23's 'that's obvious' question by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (adding the detail of awareness in between) and linking it to a specific תנא (רבן גמליאל).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first line is a plain case of one food from one dish, so it seems to teach nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first line teaches that the halves combine even with awareness in between, following רבן גמליאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the first line of the משנה is not obvious at all. It carries a real legal view about how awareness affects half-measures.

steps.title: The Source: Writing Two Letters on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: someone wrote two letters on שבת, one in the morning and one in the evening, forgetting each time. רבן גמליאל says he is liable, and the חכמים say he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If someone writes two letters while forgetting twice, one in the morning and one in the evening, רבן גמליאל says he is liable, and the חכמים say he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where רבן גמליאל's view comes from. It quotes a משנה about writing on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing two letters is the smallest amount that makes one liable for writing on שבת, so each single letter is only a half-measure. He became aware in between, yet רבן גמליאל still says he is liable. This shows he holds that the awareness did not split the two halves.

keyTerms.meaning: Morning
Evening, afternoon
Holds liable / hold exempt

phrases.english: As we learned: One who writes two letters
in two times of forgetting,
one in the morning and one in the evening:
Rabban Gamliel holds him liable,
and the Sages exempt him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַכּוֹתֵב שְׁתֵּי אוֹתִיּוֹת בִּשְׁתֵּי הֶעְלֵמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבן גמליאל that רבינא relied on in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל holds there is no awareness for a half-measure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שבת 105a about writing two letters during two times of forgetting.

steps.title: The Reason Behind the Dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל holds that awareness does not count for a half-measure. The רבנן hold that it does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל holds: Awareness does not count for a half-measure. The רבנן hold: Awareness does count for a half-measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבן גמליאל and the חכמים are really arguing about in the writing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן גמליאל, realizing the sin after only one letter means nothing, so the two letters join into one full act. For the רבנן, that awareness splits the letters into two separate times of forgetting, so neither one is a full measure and he is exempt. Our משנה about eating follows רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / they hold, as a matter of reasoning
Awareness does count for a half-measure and splits the acts

steps.whatToRemember: The first line of the משנה is about two half-כזיתים with awareness in between. It follows רבן גמליאל, who holds that awareness does not split a half-measure, so the halves combine and he is liable.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel holds:
There is no awareness for a half-measure,
and the Rabbis hold:
There is awareness for a half-measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר: אֵין יְדִיעָה לַחֲצִי שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute quoted in Step 25, which completes the support for רבינא's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל: awareness does not split a half-measure. רבנן: awareness does split a half-measure.

steps.title: New משנה: how long can the eating take
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how long one may take to eat a forbidden כזית. רבי מאיר says 'like eating קליות.' The חכמים say the whole eating must fit within the time of eating a פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long can a person take while eating forbidden food and still be liable? It is like someone eating toasted kernels, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: as long as the eating, from start to finish, fits within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a time limit for combining small bites into one punishable act of eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a כזית is not always done in one bite. The question is how spread out the bites can be and still count as one eating. רבי מאיר compares it to nibbling kernels one at a time. The חכמים give a fixed clock: the time of אכילת פרס.

keyTerms.meaning: How long may he take
Toasted grain kernels, eaten one by one
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread
Half a loaf

steps.whyThisMatters: כדי אכילת פרס becomes the standard time limit across many areas of הלכה for joining small amounts of eating together.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How long may one take while eating foods?
As though he were eating toasted kernels,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
As long as he takes, from beginning to end,
the time of eating a half-loaf, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion about half-measures and awareness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר measures the time 'as if eating קליות.' The חכמים say he is liable if the eating fits within כדי אכילת פרס.

steps.title: The half-loaf time applied to impure food and to wine in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The same כדי אכילת פרס measure applies to eating impure food, drinking impure liquids, and drinking a רביעית of wine before entering the מקדש. רבי אלעזר exempts someone who paused while drinking or added any water.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ate impure foods or drank impure liquids, the half-loaf time applies. If someone drank a quarter-log of wine, entered the Temple, and stayed there the time of eating a half-loaf, he is liable. רבי אלעזר says: if he paused while drinking, or put even a little water into the wine, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It lists more cases where the time of כדי אכילת פרס matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating impure food or drinking impure liquid makes a person unfit for תרומה. That happens only if the amount was taken within the half-loaf time. A person who drank a רביעית of wine and then entered the מקדש is liable. רבי אלעזר adds that a pause in drinking, or diluting the wine with any water, removes the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure foods
Ritually impure liquids
A quarter-log of wine
He paused (stopped) while drinking it
Any amount at all

phrases.english: If one ate impure foods
or drank impure liquids,
if he drank a quarter-log of wine
and entered the Temple
and stayed the time of eating a half-loaf, he is liable.
Rabbi Elazar says:
If he paused while drinking it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אִם נָתַן בּוֹ מַיִם כׇּל שֶׁהוּא – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: or if he put any amount of water in it, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אכל אוכלין טמאין ושתה משקין טמאין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more cases that use the same time measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure food and drink, and wine before entering the מקדש, are measured by כדי אכילת פרס. רבי אלעזר exempts the wine drinker who paused or diluted the wine.

steps.title: Is רבי מאיר being stricter or more lenient?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר's 'קליות' rule is meant לחומרא or לקולא compared to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: is רבי מאיר saying his rule to be stricter, or to be more lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the משנה. It sets up two possible readings of רבי מאיר, which the next steps lay out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like eating קליות' is unclear. It might mean that slow nibbling still counts even over a long time, which is stricter. Or it might mean the eating must be steady with no breaks, which is more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
A question was raised before them:
Rabbi Meir, is he saying it as a stringency
or is he saying it as a leniency?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of רבי מאיר's words in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's 'קליות' measure is stricter or more lenient than the חכמים' half-loaf measure.

steps.title: First possibility: רבי מאיר is being strict
steps.stepSummary: Read strictly, רבי מאיר holds that even a whole day of steady nibbling joins into one eating, even beyond the half-loaf time. The רבנן limit liability to the half-loaf time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he is being strict. His meaning: like someone nibbling kernels, even if it takes all day. Even if, from start to finish, it took longer than eating a half-loaf, he is liable, because it was one long act of eating. The רבנן answered him: he is liable only if it fits within the half-loaf time. If it takes longer, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first side of the question: רבי מאיר as the stricter view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, what matters to רבי מאיר is that the eating is one continuous act, however long it takes. The רבנן disagree. Once the eating goes past the half-loaf time, the bites no longer join, so there is no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole day
His eating was drawn out (one continuous act)
More than the time of eating a half-loaf

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי מאיר is the STRICT one. He makes a person liable even past the half-loaf time. The next step flips this.

phrases.english: He is saying it as a stringency, and this is what he teaches:
as though he were eating toasted kernels,
even if it takes the whole day.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף
phrases.english: And even though from beginning to end
it was more than the time of eating a half-loaf,
since his eating was continuous, he is liable.
And the Rabbis said to him:

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶא בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס הוּא דְּחַיָּיב
phrases.english: Only if he takes within the time of eating a half-loaf is he liable;
more than the time of eating a half-loaf, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of the question from step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי מאיר's view that continuous eating joins even beyond the half-loaf time?

steps.title: Second possibility: רבי מאיר is being lenient
steps.stepSummary: Read leniently, רבי מאיר requires steady eating with no breaks. Any pause exempts the person, even within the half-loaf time. The רבנן say that within the half-loaf time he is liable even with pauses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe he is being lenient. His meaning: like someone nibbling kernels, and only when he did not stop in between. But if he stopped in between, he is exempt, even if the whole eating fit within the half-loaf time. The רבנן answered him: since from start to finish it fit within the half-loaf time, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the second side of the question: רבי מאיר as the more lenient view. With both sides laid out, the next step tries to decide between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, רבי מאיר needs nonstop eating. A break cuts the joining, even inside the half-loaf time. For the רבנן, only the clock matters: within the half-loaf time, breaks do not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps
He paused in between

steps.whatToRemember: The question has two sides. Strict reading: for רבי מאיר, continuous eating joins even beyond the half-loaf time. Lenient reading: for רבי מאיר, any break exempts, even within the half-loaf time. In both readings, the רבנן go only by the half-loaf time.

phrases.english: Or perhaps he is saying it as a leniency,
and this is what he teaches: as though he were eating toasted kernels,
and that is only when he did not pause in between;
but if he paused in between,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִתְּחִלָּה וְעַד סוֹף
phrases.english: even though from beginning to end
it was within the time of eating a half-loaf, he is exempt.
And the Rabbis said to him:
Since from beginning to end
it is within the time of eating a half-loaf, he is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of רבי מאיר from step 30, completing the two sides of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי מאיר's view that any pause exempts, even within the half-loaf time?

steps.title: Looking at the exact wording of the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים's words in the משנה, 'עד שישהא בכדי אכילת פרס,' as a possible clue to whether רבי מאיר's view is the strict one or the lenient one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: And the חכמים say: unless he spends, from beginning to end, the amount of time it takes to eat a פרס (half a loaf).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the exact words of the משנה to try to answer its question. It is setting up a proof from the wording of the חכמים, and the reasoning will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two readings were just offered: maybe רבי מאיר is stricter, counting even a whole day of steady nibbling, or maybe he is more lenient, exempting any pause. The חכמים speak with the word 'עד' ('unless' or 'until'), which sounds like they are setting an outer limit on liability. That wording is the clue the גמרא wants to use to see which reading fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Unless/until he spends (a certain amount of time). The wording sets a boundary.
Within the time it takes to eat half a loaf of bread, the standard time limit for joining eating together.
From beginning to end. The whole eating, from the first bite to the last, is measured together.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the משנה itself, not a new ברייתא. The גמרא is not bringing new information here, only reading familiar words more closely to find a hint.

phrases.english: Come and hear: And the Rabbis say:
Unless he spends the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
from beginning to end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two possible readings (strict and lenient) were laid out, the גמרא tries to decide between them using the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי מאיר's קליות rule is לחומרא or לקולא compared to the חכמים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the חכמים in the משנה: 'עד שישהא בכדי אכילת פרס מתחלה ועד סוף,' especially the limiting word 'עד.'
